symptom: `rename page Shop.Order_Overview to Order_List` (CLI `mxcli rename page` and MDL alike) on a page in a folder named 'Order_Overview' renamed the FOLDER, left the page as it was, printed "Renamed page: …" and had already pointed every caller at the new name: mx check CE1613 "The selected page 'Shop.Order_List' no longer exists". Same for microflow, nanoflow, constant, enumeration, java action and workflow in a same-named folder; a document in a differently named folder renamed fine
cause: The handlers resolved the document among the requested kind (ListPages etc.) only to set a `found` flag, then called RenameDocumentByName(module, oldName, newName), which looked the name up AGAIN over every unit in the module's containers, whatever its $Type, and rewrote the first top-level Name that matched. A Projects$Folder is such a unit, and a FOLDER clause inserts the folder before the document it holds (Unit is a rowid table scanned in insertion order), so the folder won. The reference sweep ran before the document rename, so the damage was done whatever happened next
file: mdl/executor/cmd_rename.go (execRenameDocument, execRenameEnumeration, execRenameJavaAction); mdl/backend/modelsdk/infrastructure_write.go (RenameDocument, replacing RenameDocumentByName); mdl/backend/infrastructure.go
fix: Remove the second lookup: the handlers keep the ID of the document they found and call RenameDocument(id, oldName, newName), which refuses a Projects$Folder/ModuleImpl unit and a stored Name other than oldName. The document is renamed before the reference sweep, so a refused rename leaves every reference where it was
insight: Whether a name-only lookup hits the folder or the document is decided by unit insertion order, not by chance per run: a document created WITH a folder clause loses to its folder, one moved into an existing folder later wins — which is why the issue's enumeration/java action variants (created, then moved) looked fine on main while page/microflow/nanoflow/constant/workflow failed. A regression test must arm that order and assert it as a precondition, or it can pass against the bug. The executor had already answered the question (which document?) — passing that answer down, by ID, deletes the second resolver instead of teaching it about $Type; placement.go's FindDocumentUnit had the same lesson written down. Out of scope and still open on main: RENAME CONSTANT does not rewrite `@Module.Const` inside expressions (CE1613 at the End event, reproduced at module root with no folder) — it was masked here because the constant was never renamed
